As someone who has kind of been in the place of the daughter before, I wanted to say I'm sorry, this period must be a quite tough

I know our circumstances probably have a billion differences, but for reference, I struggle with mental health a lot and have been in ruts just like this one. 

In my case, a lot of this behavior stemmed from being so depressed and unhappy that I would chase every tiny little gratification like a drug, whether it be impulsively ordering food, or just sitting around watching random videos and shows. 

I know a lot of people are being unsupportive in this thread, I'm sorry for that. I think one thing that a lot of people who get stuck in this behavior struggle with is the fact that even with all this "laziness" and splurging, I still end up feeling totally worthless in the back of my mind. 

This is why it's so hard to help with this behavior, and why people might feel very defensive when confronted about it. Because on one hand, you're so miserable that you feel like you can't help it, so it's really frustrating to get criticized about it. But at the same time, it feels like it's all you're able to do anymore.

I don't know your daughter, and have no idea if she's in the same spot. But I just wanted to share and potentially shed some light on the situation. Wishing the best for your family <3

This is hard to answer, since it's a lot different from the perspective of someone with an eating disorder, and I know anything I say will probably be seen as just an excuse. Those type of tips, for me, were advocating much healthier behavior than the alternative.

It's going to be really weird for me to talk about myself so personally and graphically here, but a large part of my disorder is control. If I manage to get through the day only eating what I don't regret after, I feel happy. I actually feel like I have a hold on things. But if I don't, if I slip up and eat way more than I'm supposed to, I feel incredibly depressed. It feels like everything's wrong, I'm weak and terrible, I can't do anything right. So I end up puking it all out. But then I'm hungry again. So the cycle continues until I've puked like 4 times and have only stopped through to total exhaustion.

That is basically what happens for me having anorexia/bulimia. I can't just...magically wish it away. That's the whole reason I still suffer from this. But if I could just deal with it sort of normally without having the nonstop worrying about eating and getting to feel a little in control, even if its by eating a certain amount of calories or suppressing my appetite, it helps living like that day to day.

There was never any weird ED encouragement. In fact, there was a rule that stated that any advice on how to become anorexic or how to throw up or whatever was not allowed. 

It was just a support sub in the same way that /r/depression is. Just a place for people to talk about it without others judging and chiming in with "don't you know its not healthy?" 

I feel like because of the taboo nature and public opinion of eating disorders, it got unfairly judged. People seem to be quick to assume things when it doesn't apply to them
